headline: Commentary: The vote is mightier than the map …
summary: A recent poll by Elon University's School of Communications found that a majority of North Carolinians disapprove of the job performance of Governor Roy Cooper and the state legislature, with 52% and 57% disapproval respectively. The poll also revealed that 64% of respondents support the state's expansion of Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act, a key policy debate in North Carolina.

headline: Voters Said Yes To Food Security Fund. How Will Honolulu Spend It?
summary: Poll finds majority of Hawaii voters support both existing programs and trying new approaches.

headline: Idaho Legislature’s budget committee meets in Moscow, Lewiston this week
summary: The Joint Finance-Appropriations Committee (JFAC), Idaho's key budget committee, is preparing for the 2027 legislative session by holding meetings in Moscow and Lewiston, focusing on budget briefings, audits, and facility tours. Last year, JFAC cut most state agency budgets by 4% and 5% for FY 2026 and FY 2027 respectively, except for K-12 schools. The committee will begin working on the FY 2028 budget in January.

headline: Dozens sue for justice for alleged ICE abuse during Operation Metro Surge
summary: Ten months after U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent Jonathan Ross fatally shot Renee Good in Minneapolis, no criminal charges have been filed. The Good family, along with dozens of others, is seeking justice through civil courts using the Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA), as there's no federal law allowing citizens to sue federal agents for constitutional violations. The FTCA has limitations, including caps on payouts and attorneys' fees, and doesn't allow suing for constitutional rights violations. Lawyers hope these lawsuits will deter ICE's "brutal tactics" and bring accountability.

headline: RI budget and policy director Brian Daniels resigns
summary: Brian Daniels, Rhode Island's Office of Management and Budget Director, resigns after contributing to twelve budgets under three governors. His accomplishments include creating a state supplemental rainy day fund and using federal COVID relief funds for capital projects, leading to a bond rating upgrade. Governor-elect Helena Foulkes will fill the vacancy as she plans her first budget proposal.

headline: Gov. Evers joins criminal justice advocates at EXPO gala
summary: The event commemorated the joint anniversary of EXPO and The Community, celebrating criminal justice reform, commutations, and support for formerly incarcerated individuals. Gov. Tony Evers was present, acknowledging his support for criminal justice reform and commutations.

headline: School referendum passage declines amid public school advocates’ high hopes for new state government
summary: Wisconsin voters approved fewer school referendums than previous years, with around 55% passing, impacting districts' budgets. State Superintendent Jill Underly calls for changes to the school funding formula, as 62% of schools face reduced aid for 2026-27. Incoming Democratic leaders plan to increase school funding but may also establish a blue ribbon commission to study taxation and school funding, drawing criticism from some advocates who want immediate action.

headline: Michigan voters support more education funding, but how to pay for it is complicated
summary: A public opinion poll commissioned by the K-12 Alliance of Michigan found that half of surveyed voters believed their local school districts had funding shortages.
